# MorrowTab

> MorrowTab is a Chrome and Edge extension that replaces the new-tab page with a board-based homepage: columns of organized links, a search box that uses your browser's own default provider or extra engines you add yourself, and a daily FixQuotes quote. Boards, columns, links, search engines and shared settings travel through the browser's own extension sync, with no MorrowTab account or server holding that synced graph. The separate website-icon feature sends eligible saved hostnames to FixQuotes to retrieve public icons; it does not send complete saved addresses or titles.

MorrowTab is published by FixQuotes and is available from Microsoft Edge Add-ons: https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/pbdbhkiajaobdacbebifndnghiiodlgi. Its Chrome Web Store listing is coming soon. Requirements are Chrome or Edge on Chromium 114 or newer.

Use the user manual for detailed information about boards, columns and links, search engines and URL templates, the Quick Save toolbar popup, keyboard shortcuts, themes and backgrounds, the four daily-quote modes, backup and restore, the enforced storage limits, and the read-only recovery view.

## Key facts

- Platform: MorrowTab is a Manifest V3 extension for Chrome and Edge.
- Browsers: Chrome or Edge on Chromium 114 or newer. The floor exists because MorrowTab uses the Popover API, Web Locks, CSS `:has()` and CSS `color-mix()`. There is no Firefox, Safari or mobile version.
- Availability: as of 2 September 2026 MorrowTab is published on Microsoft Edge Add-ons at https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/pbdbhkiajaobdacbebifndnghiiodlgi. Its Chrome Web Store listing is not live yet. This site offers no direct download or side-load instructions, and there is no public source repository.
- Account: none. No sign-up, no login, no MorrowTab-hosted copy of the synced board graph. Boards, columns, links, search engines and shared settings live in the browser's own extension sync (chrome.storage.sync), which is not end-to-end encrypted, so saved names, titles and addresses should be treated as non-confidential.
- Network hosts: exactly three fixed hosts, for switchable features — `https://fixquotes.com` for the daily quote feed, `https://api.fixquotes.com` for daily nature-background metadata and website-icon lookup, and `https://images.pexels.com` for photo bytes. The daily quote is ON by default (Text mode) and fetches once per local day; setting it to Off stops its request. Nature photos are enabled by `backgroundMode: "pexels"` only in the bundled fresh starter, including its read-only preview, so new sample setups and previews may request the public FixQuotes/Pexels background endpoints. Turning the nature setting off stops background requests but does not change the separate icon-download preference. Existing synced/imported background settings remain unchanged; an absent or explicit `theme` background mode stays off. A further direct site request is possible only after two separate opt-ins: turning on "Fetch page titles when adding links" (off by default) and then granting Chrome's per-site permission prompt for the one address being added.
- Website icons: "Download website icons" defaults to ON locally. A working bundled brand needs no request; otherwise MorrowTab can POST only the exact hostname (including subdomain/www) to `https://api.fixquotes.com/public/morrowtab/favicon` as JSON, with no saved path, query, title, credentials, cookies or referrer. FixQuotes obtains public-site artwork directly and returns a verified 32×32 PNG, without a third-party favicon provider. Native generic-globe success does not block lookup. The local cache is limited to 128 entries/256 KiB, seven-day freshness, a 30-day stale-use limit, and 24-hour caching for explicit no-icon/blocked results. Transport failures begin with a five-minute retry delay, exponential backoff capped at 24 hours, and a shared cooldown. Switching downloads off stops new requests and keeps cached icons. Private literals and obvious internal/reserved names are rejected, but public-looking intranet hostnames cannot reliably be identified; disable before showing sensitive internal links if hostname disclosure to FixQuotes is unsuitable. Fixed POST routing keeps the hostname out of application request URLs, not necessarily infrastructure/body logs.
- Permissions declared: storage, favicon, search, activeTab and alarms, optional webNavigation for link auto-close, the three fixed host permissions above, plus an optional `https://*/*` host permission that is never granted at install and is requested one origin at a time for the page-title fetch.
- Auto-close permission is per installation, while configured link timeouts sync. Saving an enabled timeout or first opening a synced timed link can offer the missing optional navigation permission from that user action. Declining while opening still opens a normal tab without auto-close and without an error warning. A local Boolean remembers the first offer, avoiding repeated automatic prompts across new tabs and reloads. The neutral "Enable auto-close" notice action explicitly retries for future timed openings; Open all shares one pending request. Already-granted access does not prompt, and declining editor Save leaves the link unchanged.
- Storage limits (enforced before every write, nothing is unlimited): 30 boards; 120 columns total and 40 per board; 250 links total and 200 per column; 80 additional search engines total and 20 per board; and a sync budget of 500 records, 8,000 bytes per record and 100,000 bytes in total. Text caps: board name 80 characters, column title 100, link title 160, link description 200, search-engine name 80, and 2,048 characters for a URL or search template.
- Stays on one computer and never syncs or appears in a backup: the selected board, the Quick Save destination, saved search suggestions and their on/off preference, an uploaded background image, the cached nature photo, the cached daily quote, two local safety snapshots, the managed-tab fail-closed marker, the auto-close permission-prompt marker, downloaded favicon images with hostname/expiry metadata, and the favicon-download preference. The separate random schema-2 actor identity brings the local-record total to fourteen; it is excluded from backups but also appears as pseudonymous causal metadata in this profile's synced checkpoint. Live managed-tab IDs, hostnames and countdowns remain session-only and are not synced or exported.
- Backup: Settings exports the synced records to a plaintext JSON file on that computer. Importing a full backup replaces all synced data after confirmation; importing a single exported column adds it to the current board instead.
- Search: "Browser default" hands the query to the provider the Chrome or Edge profile is already set to. MorrowTab never changes the browser's default engine and ships with no search provider preconfigured. Search suggestions come only from the user's own completed searches, stored on that computer.
- No analytics, telemetry or tracking script exists in the extension, and this website has no analytics and no consent banner.
- The first-install welcome asks new users to start with the 50-link "Popular websites" sample board or returning users to open their existing synced boards without publishing the sample. Empty Sync is otherwise a read-only preview until the user explicitly chooses the sample.
- "Boardmark" is not a product name. It survives only as an import alias for files exported before the rename.
